subject.title: Feature: configurable LLM retry with backoff on transient errors (overloaded/529)

question: What public retry/backoff contract should OpenClaw expose for main LLM requests: provider-level, agent/global, both, or no new config surface?
rationale: This changes public configuration and provider/fallback runtime behavior; automation can inspect gaps, but it cannot choose the permanent API, idempotency boundary, or user-visible retry semantics safely.

options.title: Settle provider retry contract first
options.body: Use the canonical issue to define provider retry fields only if maintainers require end-to-end runtime wiring, fallback ordering, docs, and tests before merge.

options.title: Design an agent/global policy
options.body: Hold provider-level config and specify an agents.defaults-style policy with retry classes, custom backoff, total cap, and notification behavior.

options.title: Reject new retry config for now
options.body: Keep existing failover, auth cooldown, same-model rate-limit, and cron retry behavior, and close the feature direction only after maintainers explicitly reject the extra config surface.

recommendation.title: Settle provider retry contract first
recommendation.body: Use the canonical issue to define provider retry fields only if maintainers require end-to-end runtime wiring, fallback ordering, docs, and tests before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc has the strongest current routing signal across provider request config, model-provider transport, release/provider runtime history, and adjacent retry/failover review context.
